title: The ladder's shape and the stone as temple and gate
english: So if we think about it, we can see that some people sometimes call the very sufferings of temptations by the name of steep rugged ascents and descents, paths with cliffs on both sides. Yet in shape the ladder does in some small way resemble the cross, fitted together with upright and crosswise timbers. When Jacob had beheld this vision, he took the stone on which he had reclined his head and rested, and he set it up as a pillar as a memorial of the event. He also made it an image characterizing the person who had appeared to him, and in it he established a renewal of remembrance. By calling it the house of God, he was hinting at the temple of God's Word, as the Son of the Almighty himself declared: "Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up" (John 2:19). He also named the same stone the gate of heaven, because through the temple-building of Christ we are cleansed in body and soul, and so we are able to approach the divine nature.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: Eustathius is explaining how the details of Jacob's vision and pillar at Bethel prefigure Christ, the cross, and the church.

title: The oil and the stone as signs of Christ's anointing, burial, and cornerstone
english: So he did not pour the oil on the top of the pillar without purpose. Rather, it pointed to what Mary was doing earnestly when she poured ointment upon the extremities, the feet of Christ. And that oil, in turn, happened to be a sign of the burial, as the Lord himself made clear openly. This stone images that cornerstone which the builders rejected, but which became the cornerstone (Psalm 117:22). The divine Scriptures reveal two nations and two peoples. Moses is a witness to this. In Genesis, when he narrates the life of Rebecca, he says that she went to inquire of the Lord about what she had conceived.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: Eustathius is explaining the prophetic meaning of the details of Jacob's pillar at Bethel, now turning to the oil poured on it and the stone itself.

title: The Two Peoples and the Younger's Dominion
english: Then he says: The Lord said to her, “Two nations are in your womb, and two peoples will be separated from your body; one people will surpass the other, and the greater will serve the lesser” (Genesis 25:23). For there are many nations and many peoples, but these two in particular are called peoples, because they were deemed worthy to be entrusted with the teaching of piety. He makes no mention of schisms or heresies or those that would be numbered. Rather, there are two peoples stretched out across much of the earth: Christians and Jews. The greater, boasting in its antiquity, is left behind in virtue and will serve the younger; for, as Scripture says, “the fool will serve the wise”. From this, then, he prefigured him sitting upon the throne of the Holy One, showing that he has been demonstrated to be enthroned together with the most divine Spirit because God dwells in him continually.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: Eustathius is closing his treatise by interpreting the Lord's words to Rebecca about the two nations in her womb as a prophecy of Jews and Christians, with the older people serving the younger.
